AdExtendedId.description:
A single extended identifier from a CxM identity vendor, following the OpenRTB 2.6 eids spec.
See: https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-6.pdf

Supported vendors:
- SharedID / PubCommon: source="pubcid.org", agentType=1
- ID5:                  source="id5-sync.com", agentType=1
- Lotame Panorama ID:   source="crwdcntrl.net", agentType=1
- LiveRamp ATS:         source="liveramp.com", agentType=3

inputFields.description:
The vendor domain that is the source of the identifier
(e.g. 'id5-sync.com', 'pubcid.org', 'crwdcntrl.net', 'liveramp.com').
inputFields.name: source

inputFields.description:
The user IDs from this source. These are different than the standard urXXXX within IMDb, see WebAdExtendedIdUserId.
There will be one userId per AdExtendedId, but we keep the array data structure to match what's expected in the
OpenRTB spec: https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/OpenRTB-API-Specification-Version-2-6.pdf

No maximum array size, we will always use the first value in the array downstream

Example: userIds: [{ id: "AsvkAsvQTfYZNRVUbs0LJ1C5Tti...", agentType: 3 }]
inputFields.name: userIds

AdExtendedId.name: AdExtendedId

AdExtendedIdUserId.description:
A single user ID within an extended identifier.

Example: { id: "e52a-4033-b54c-f67d", agentType: 1 }

inputFields.description:
The agent type of the ID per OpenRTB 2.6 atype enum.
Valid values: 1 (device/cookie-based), 2 (in-app impression-based), 3 (person-based).
Unrecognized values will be forwarded as-is to downstream buyers.
We map this to `atype` downstream in IMDbAdsGraphlet -> PAS -> AAX

OpenRTB/AdCOM standard defines the values for agentType here:
https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/AdCOM/blob/main/AdCOM%20v1.0%20FINAL.md#list_agenttypes

Examples: 1 for SharedID/ID5/Lotame, 3 for LiveRamp. Possible values include 1, 2, or 3
inputFields.name: agentType

inputFields.description: The user ID value
inputFields.name: id

Gross revenue pulled in via box-office in Domestic market for entire lifetime of title.
Domestic refers to North America (U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico)
ASC: Lower numbers means the title has pulled in less box-office revenue, so poorer performing titles will be first.

enumValues.description:
Overall Metascore based on critic reviews. Titles without a metascore are
placed at the end when using ASC sort order.
ASC: Lower Metacritic score means the title is rated more poorly, so titles with worse scores will be first.
enumValues.name: METACRITIC_SCORE

enumValues.description:
Star Rating given by the requesting user.
ASC: Lower star rating means the title the user rated the title more poorly, so most disliked titles will be first.
enumValues.name: MY_RATING

enumValues.description:
Date when customer rated a title.
ASC: Earlier (older) ratings will be first.
enumValues.name: MY_RATING_DATE

enumValues.description:
Date when the requesting customer watched a title.
Throws UNAUTHENTICATED if the requesting customer is not authenticated.
ASC: Earlier (older) watched dates will be first.
enumValues.name: MY_WATCHED_DATE

enumValues.description:
TitleMeterType.TITLE_METER (aka Pro MOVIEMeter). Score given to non-episodic title types.
ASC: Lower popularity score means that the title is more popular, so the most popular titles will be first.
enumValues.name: POPULARITY

enumValues.description:
Sort based on production status update time.
ASC: Titles with older status updates will be placed first (least recently updated first)
DESC: Titles with newer status updates will be placed first (most recently updated first)
enumValues.name: PRODUCTION_STATUS_UPDATE_DAYS

enumValues.description:
Sort results based on specified ranking algorithm.  For the advancedTitleSearch query, exactly one ranked title list
constraint must be specified for using this sort option.
ASC: Higher ranks will be first.
enumValues.name: RANKING

enumValues.description:
Earliest wide release date of a title. Titles without a release date are
placed at the end when using ASC sort order.
ASC: Earlier (older) released title will be first.
enumValues.name: RELEASE_DATE

enumValues.description:
The length of the title in terms of runtime.
ASC: Lower runtime means the title is shorter, so shortest titles will be first.
enumValues.name: RUNTIME

enumValues.description:
Star Rating given by the specified user in the SpecifiedUserRatingSearchConstraint.
Throws BAD_USER_INPUT if the SpecifiedUserRatingSearchConstraint is not specified.
ASC: Lower star rating means the title the user rated the title more poorly, so most disliked titles will be first.
enumValues.name: SINGLE_USER_RATING

enumValues.description:
Date when the specified user rated a title.
Throws BAD_USER_INPUT if the SpecifiedUserRatingSearchConstraint is not specified.
ASC: Earlier (older) ratings will be first.
enumValues.name: SINGLE_USER_RATING_DATE

enumValues.description:
Date when the specified user watched a title.
Throws BAD_USER_INPUT if the SingleUserWatchedSearchConstraint is not specified.
ASC: Earlier (older) watched dates will be first.

enumValues.description:
Alphabetical sorting based on regional title text as determined by user language preferences.
Language preference is determined by x-imdb-user-country and x-imdb-user-language headers.
Only supports the languages/regions we support for localized search. Defaults to original title otherwise.
ASC: Lower numbers and letters near the top of the alphabet will be returned first.
enumValues.name: TITLE_REGIONAL

enumValues.description:

CharacterSearchConstraint.description:
Example:
1. if you want to match titles with character name ('Micky Mouse' OR 'Pluto')
specify anyCharacterName: ['Micky Mouse', 'Pluto'].

2. if you want to match titles where name const ('nm0000138') played a character called ('Jordan')
specify characterSearchConstraint: { anyCharacterName: ['Jordan'], shouldLimitToCreditedNameIds: true } and
creditedNameConstraint: { anyNameIds: ['nm0000138'] }

inputFields.description: A title match must contain AT LEAST ONE of these character names.
inputFields.name: anyCharacterNames

inputFields.description:
If this is set to true when a CreditedNameConstraint anyNameIds, or allNameIds is specified, then a title match
must contain AT LEAST ONE of these character names, where AT LEAST ONE of the name ids
is playing them.

the constraint will behave the same whether anyNameIds or allNameIds were used, meaning
characterSearchConstraint: { anyCharacterName: ['Jordan'], shouldLimitToCreditedNameIds: true } and
creditedNameConstraint: { anyNameIds: ['nm1706767', 'nm0000138', 'nm0000190'] } will return the same results
if anyNameIds was replaced with allNameIds, and specifying both allNameIds and anyNameIds will just combine the
name ids that are matched against the specified characters.
inputFields.name: shouldLimitToCreditedNameIds

fields.description:
The employees of this company — people who work at the company in
some capacity (e.g. agents, legal representatives, managers).

Not all companies have employee information.

Will return an empty set of edges if we have no employee information for
the company.

Employees are returned in the order they appear in IMDb's underlying
company employees record (in practice, ascending by name ID). No other
ordering is applied or guaranteed.

Up to 250 employees can be requested at a time. If `first` is greater
than 250, only 250 employees will be returned.

If `after` is omitted, results start from the beginning of the list.

Returns a connection with empty `edges` and a `total` of 0 when the
customer is not entitled, including when the customer is not logged in.

inputFields.description:
Defines how credits are aggregated together into a single CreditV2 result.

Aggregation allows clients to choose the level of detail to show for credits, avoiding repetition of the same
named individual across many roles or appearances.

Parameter is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

NAME: All credits for a single name on a single title are aggregated together.
This supports experiences like Filmmakers tab on pro.imdb.com, where all work by a name within a category is
shown together.
For example, see Hugh Wilson in https://pro.imdb.com/title/tt0116130/filmmakers.

NAME_WITHOUT_ORDERABLE_GROUPS: All credits for a single name on a single title are aggregated together,
except for groupings that support hierarchies (for example the Writer grouping). For these, aggregation is disabled.
This allows for the hierarchy of writer credits to be vended, capturing a single writer's individual contributions
to a title in the correct order.
For example, see Hugh Wilson in https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116130/fullcredits/#writer.

NAME_AND_GROUPING: All credits of the same grouping and the same single name on a single title are aggregated together.
inputFields.name: aggregationType

inputFields.description:
Capture the order of CreditGrouping items in a listing.

This is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

CREDIT_GROUPING_IMPORTANCE: Credit grouping ordering follows this priority sequence:
1. Profession - The credit categories associated with the name's professions, in profession order
2. Fixed grouping order for additional and passive appearances - Credit
groupings that capture when a name is appearing as Self,
or where they were not actively involved in the title (such as Thanks or
Archive credits) are moved to the end of the ordering
3. Credit count - The number of credits a name has within the grouping, largest first
4. Fixed grouping order - A fixed order, presenting groupings in an order similar to that seen on movie or TV
end credits.

CREDIT_GROUPING_IMPORTANCE is the default.

The sort order can be controlled using the order parameter (ASC/DESC). When DESC (default), primary professions
and high-credit-count groupings appear first. When ASC, passive appearances and low-credit-count groupings appear first.

CreditHierarchy.description:
Captures details of the hierarchy of credits, for credit groups that support a hierarchy.
Two examples where this exists today:
* Writer (https://help.imdb.com/article/contribution/filmography-credits/writers/GPLAT3NTCGA67A6R#)
  * This category supports a three-level hierarchy. The levels are named
"WriterFamily", "WriterTeam", and "WriterTeamMember".
  * Documentation below shows examples of this hierarchy
* Cast (https://help.imdb.com/article/contribution/filmography-credits/how-are-cast-credits-ordered-why-don-t-the-main-stars-appear-at-the-top-of-the-cast/G39K5N4YYV2QJ4GR)
  * These credits are vended as a collection of ordered credits, followed by a collection of unordered credits.
    Our hierarchy here is therefore one level deep, with up to two expected levelKeys at that level.
  * Concretely we would see a hierarchy of the form:

    [Root]
      /\
     /  \
    A    B        # CastGrouping
   /|    /|\
  / |   / | \
 C  D  E  F  G    # CastMember

 * In this example, C and D would be cast members with an order number associated with them. E, F, G would have no
   associated order, and so are in the second CastGrouping.

fields.description:
Informs clients when to use the filterKeys in hierarchy levelDetails for
the given filter. hierarchyFilter is an enum for available filters that a hierarchy can use.
So for locale it would be `hierarchyFilter: "LOCALE"`. When the hierarchyFilter field is null
then the hierarchy is not filterable.
fields.name: hierarchyFilter

fields.description:
For each non-leaf node in our hierarchy, provide a count for the number of child nodes.
Allows a client to look at an individual credit record and understand its relative position in the hierarchy,
without knowledge of the hierarchy itself.
For example, given the following hierarchy:

[Root]
|
A
| \
B  C
|  | \
D  E  F

If a client is rendering the credit F, they can determine that F is the last credit within the C subtree,
because:
* This group of credits is vended with `hierarchy` containing:
  `{ "levels": ["WriterFamily", "WriterTeam", "WriterTeamMember"],
     "levelDetails": [
       { "levelsKey": "WriterFamily[0].WriterTeam[0]", childCount: 1 },
       { "levelsKey": "WriterFamily[0].WriterTeam[1]", childCount: 2 },
     ]
   }`
* F is vended with `hierarchyDetail` of
  `[ { "level": "WriterFamily", "position": 0 }, { "level": "WriterTeam",
"position": 1 }, { "level": "WriterTeamMember", "position": 1 } ]`
* A client can see that within "WriterFamily[0].WriterTeam[1]", F's WriterTeamMember-level position (2) matches the
  total childCount for that node in the `hierarchy` data.
fields.name: levelDetails

fields.description:
Ordered list of levels. Allows a client to understand the content of `levelDetails`,
and the `hierarchyDetails` against a grouped credit edge (see CreditGroupingEdge).
For the Writer group this would return `["WriterFamily", "WriterTeam", "WriterTeamMember"]`.
fields.name: levels

CreditHierarchy.name: CreditHierarchy

CreditHierarchyDetail.description:
Captures an individual CreditV2's position within a credit group's hierarchy.
This type captures the position within a single level of the hierarchy.
An array of these can identify a credit's unique position within a multi-level hierarchy.
Values are zero-indexed.
For example, for the Writer credit group (with levels "WriterFamily", "WriterTeam", "WriterTeamMember"),
and hierarchy of shape:

      [Root]
      |
      A          # WriterFamily
     / \
    /   \
   B     C       # WriterTeam
  /|    /|\
 / |   / | \
D  E  F  G  H    # WriterTeamMember

Node "F" would have values:
`[
   { "level": "WriterFamily", "position": 0 },
   { "level": "WriterTeam", "position": 1 },
   { "level": "WriterTeamMember", "position": 0 }
 ]`

fields.description: Name of the level of hierarchy we are giving a position for.
fields.name: level

fields.description:
This credit's relative position within this level of the hierarchy.
Values are zero-indexed.
Considers sibling nodes under the same parent, and not other nodes from the same level but
with different parents.
fields.name: position

CreditHierarchyDetail.name: CreditHierarchyDetail

fields.description:
Count of the number of children beneath this node in the hierarchy.
Does not count children of children.
In the example above, the childCount for node "C" is 2 (counting nodes "E" and "F").
fields.name: childCount

fields.description:
A key that should be used as a filter value when `hierarchyFilter` is not null.
The filterKey will be unique across the levelDetails. This field may be empty for hierarchies that
are not used as filters like the cast and writer hierarchies.
fields.name: filterKey

fields.description:
Unique ID for this displayable text.
ID will encode the titleId for this title as well as `levelsKey`, as each
title can have different headers for their hierarchies.
Required as part of LocalizedDisplayableConcept interface to support caching.
fields.name: id

fields.description:
Identifies a single node in a hierarchy, in xpath-like syntax
For the three-level Writer hierarchy, a levelsKey value would be "WriterFamily[0].WriterTeam[1]".
This corresponds to node "C" in the following hierarchy:

[Root]
|
A
| \
B  C
|  | \
D  E  F

We only represent nodes with children with a CreditHierarchyLevelDetail. Leaf nodes would not be
expected to have a value, since their childCount is always zero.
Null values are possible, for credit groups that have no inherent hierarchy but do have text to associate with
the credits. For example in Writers grouping, a series of hierarchical credits can be followed by unordered credits.
These are vended with no levelsKey but with other fields like text populated.
fields.name: levelsKey

fields.description:
Descriptive text for this level of the hierarchy.
For Cast, we could expect en-US text of the form "(in credits order) verified as complete" and

CreditV2.description:
Details of a credit for a name on a title. Distinct from Company Credits or Crazy Credits.
Successor to Credit type.
Denotes the role(s) a person had on a title.
Fields within this record may be aggregations or summaries of work done, depending on how the data was requested.

When requesting credits for a series, roles performed on the episodes of that series are rolled up to the series level.
Each rolled-up role comes with its own listing of the episodes that the role was performed on.
If the attributes of a role are not shared across all episodes, we drop that detail.
* Example: Kaley Cuoco (nm0192505) was credited as Kaley Cuoco-Sweeting for some but not all episodes of
The Big Bang Theory (tt0898266). When viewing credits at the series level, this attribute is dropped. The attribute
is still present at an episode level.

Characters and CreditedRoles for a series are ordered by most recent value first. This ensures a person's most recent
contribution to a title (and so the work they are most likely to demonstrate their skillset) is shown first.
This also helps to highlight the roles that users are likely to be exploring, particularly for long-running shows
where acting roles change over time (for example, Saturday Night Live).
Note that the ordering of these fields differs when using name.knownForV2 (see its documentation for details).

Appearance credits (such as acting and self-appearances) are contributed to IMDb's catalog as a single credit per title.
* Example: Ryan Reynolds (nm0005351) plays Deadpool and Nicepool in Deadpool & Wolverine (tt6263850).
This is different to crew credits, where a single person can have many roles on a title, even within a single
credit category.
* Example: Hugh Wilson (nm0933505) is both screenplay and story writer for Down Periscope (tt0116130), and these are
captured in the catalog as separate credits.

The CreditV2 shape maintains this distinction. For appearance credits, the individual roles played can be accessed
individually from the `CreditV2.creditedRoles.characters` field.

When a person performs different appearance roles across episodes in a TV series, we maintain this cast-specific
difference in data shape. All appearance work is aggregated into a single CreditV2 entry, with a single
`creditedRoles.text` value that includes up to 100 roles, and all roles available in the `characters` field.
* Example: Kaley Cuoco (nm0192505) plays two different roles across episodes in The Big Bang Theory (tt0898266).
This is vended at the series level as a single credit with one `creditedRoles.text` ("Penny/Penny Hofstatder") and
two character values (["Penny", "Penny Hofstatder"]).
Character names are ordered by their frequency across episodes, then by which occurs first in release order.

- Single ID: a 1:1 mapping between this credit and a single catalog entry.

  (e.g., episode credits rolled up to the series level, where each constituent episode credit

inputFields.description:
Captures the ordering of credited roles within a CreditV2. This ensures consistent ordering of roles
when a name has performed many different roles on a title. This is often seen on long-running series.

This is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

CREDITED_ROLE_IMPORTANCE: Credit ordering follows this priority sequence:
1. Profession - The credit categories associated with the name's professions, in profession order
2. Latest release date - For series, most recent episode release date that this credit applies to
3. Episode count - For a series, higher episode counts appear first
4. Credited status - Credited roles take precedence over uncredited
5. Role - Alphabetical comparison of the credited role text
6. Title ID - A final tie-break by episode title ID to ensure consistent ordering (largest first)

CREDITED_ROLE_IMPORTANCE is the default.

The sort order can be controlled using the order parameter.

fields.description:
The requesting customer's own standing in this leaderboard.

Throws UNAUTHENTICATED if not logged in.
Returns null if the customer has earned no points in this scope.
fields.name: myStanding

fields.description:
Ranked entries, ordered by points descending. Tied users share the same rank (competition ranking).
Supports two pagination modes (mutually exclusive):
- `after`: Forward pagination from the top (standard Relay cursor).
- `aroundProfileId`: Centers the page on the given user's position — returns
  floor(first/2) entries above, the user, and the remaining below.

When both `after` and `aroundProfileId` are omitted, pagination starts from rank 1.

At most 100 entries per page; first is capped at 100 (smaller values return that many).
Pass first: 0 to fetch only the connection `total` (page metadata) with no ranking edges.

Users who have not earned points in this scope do not appear in the rankings; passing
their profileId to `aroundProfileId` throws RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND (no position to center on).

Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if first is less than 0.
Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if both `after` and `aroundProfileId` are provided.
Throws RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if `aroundProfileId` references a user with no ranking in this leaderboard.
fields.name: rankings

enumValues.description:

enumValues.description:
Pro signup button on the second Pro PAP → AAP conversion interstitial
(SHOW_PRO_PAP_TO_AAP_CONVERSION second variant). Client performs the cookie swap and
navigates to /signup/pro/start?pap_cnvrt=<value> to begin the Pro signup flow.
pap_cnvrt is a base64-encoded string in the same format as the siteState value on an
AuthPortal sign-in URL.
enumValues.name: CONTINUE_TO_PRO_SIGNUP

enumValues.description:
"Continue with IMDb" button on the SHOW_AMAZON_ACCOUNT_IN_USE_INTERSTITIAL error interstitial.
Client calls recordAmazonAccountPoolConversionDecline(reason: AMAZON_ACCOUNT_IN_USE) →
120-day TTL before PAP sign-in completes. The Amazon account entered during conversion is
already linked to a different IMDb account.
enumValues.name: CONTINUE_WITH_IMDB

enumValues.description:
Convert an IMDb account that has existing LWA linkage to the authenticated Amazon account.
Client should call conversion mutation with just the Amazon token.
enumValues.name: CONVERT_LWA_TO_AAP

enumValues.description:
Convert the authenticated IMDb account to the authenticated Amazon account.
Client should call conversion mutation with both tokens.
enumValues.name: CONVERT_TO_AAP

enumValues.description:
Create new IMDb account using authenticated Amazon account.
Client should proceed with new account creation.
enumValues.name: CREATE_NEW_ACCOUNT

enumValues.description:
Decline the PAP-to-AAP conversion offer.
Client should record the decline (60-day TTL) and complete sign-in normally.
enumValues.name: DECLINE_CONVERSION

enumValues.description:
Home page banner "Get started" button.
Navigates to /registration/conversion/?conversionMode=INITIATE, bypassing the TTL check.
enumValues.name: INITIATE_CONVERSION

enumValues.description:
Start IMDb account linking process.
Client should initiate the IMDb authentication flow for linking.
enumValues.name: LINK_IMDB_ACCOUNT

enumValues.description:
Start IMDb account linking process.
Client should initiate the IMDb authentication flow for linking with a prefilled email.
enumValues.name: LINK_IMDB_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_PREFILLED

enumValues.description:
Return user to sign-in options.
Client should navigate to the main sign-in options page/screen.
enumValues.name: SHOW_SIGN_IN_OPTIONS

enumValues.description:
Redirect user to Amazon (AAP) sign-in flow.
Client should navigate to the Sign in with Amazon page/screen.
Used for standard Amazon account authentication.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_AMAZON

enumValues.description:
Redirect user to Amazon linking sign-in flow.
Client should navigate to the platform-appropriate imdb_amazon_linking association handle.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_AMAZON_LINKING

enumValues.description:
3P deprecation interstitial primary button. Web and iOS only.
Apple sign-in is not supported on Android — this value is never returned for Android handles.
Returned on SHOW_3P_DEPRECATION_INTERSTITIAL for imdb_apple (web) and imdb_mobile_ios_apple (iOS).
Client routes to AuthPortal / MAP SDK with the platform-appropriate Apple handle.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_APPLE

enumValues.description:
"Sign in with Apple to verify" button on the conversionMode: INITIATE interstitial variant.
Shown when the PAP user has Apple auth linked — web and iOS only (Apple unavailable on Android).
Determined via userLinkedAuthProvidersDataLoader at render time.
Client routes to: Web: imdb_apple_linking · iOS: imdb_mobile_ios_apple_linking.
RAR returns immediateAction: SIGN_IN_WITH_AMAZON_LINKING → zero-UI redirect.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_APPLE_LINKING

enumValues.description:
3P deprecation interstitial primary button. Web, iOS, and Android.
Returned on SHOW_3P_DEPRECATION_INTERSTITIAL for imdb_google (web),
imdb_mobile_ios_google (iOS), and imdb_mobile_android_google (Android).
Client routes to AuthPortal / MAP SDK with the platform-appropriate Google handle.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_GOOGLE

enumValues.description:
"Sign in with Google to verify" button on the conversionMode: INITIATE interstitial variant.
Shown when the PAP user has Google auth linked — all platforms.
Determined via userLinkedAuthProvidersDataLoader at render time.
Client routes to: Web: imdb_google_linking · iOS: imdb_mobile_ios_google_linking · Android: imdb_mobile_android_google_linking.
RAR returns immediateAction: SIGN_IN_WITH_AMAZON_LINKING → zero-UI redirect.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_GOOGLE_LINKING

enumValues.description:
Redirect user to IMDb sign-in flow.
Client should navigate to the Sign in with IMDb page/screen.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_IMDB

enumValues.description:
Button on the email match conversion interstitial.
Redirects to the platform-appropriate email match linking association handle
(imdb_email_match_linking, imdb_mobile_ios_email_match_linking, or
imdb_mobile_android_email_match_linking). The client navigates to AuthPortal with
the Amazon token in the primary cookie — the server resolves the PAP account from
the linking cookie and initiates the email match AAP conversion flow.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_IMDB_EMAIL_MATCH_LINKING

enumValues.description:
Redirect user to IMDb sign-in flow with a prefilled email.
Client should navigate to the Sign in with IMDb page/screen.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_IMDB_EMAIL_PREFILLED

enumValues.description:
"Sign in to verify" button on the conversionMode: INITIATE interstitial variant.
Redirects to the imdb_us_linking association handle. RAR returns SIGN_IN_WITH_AMAZON_LINKING
(zero-UI). Always shown as the default verify option for all users — no credential check required.
Shown alongside any 3P verify buttons determined by userLinkedAuthProvidersDataLoader.

enumValues.description:
Redirect user to LWA sign-in flow.
Client should navigate to the Sign in with Amazon page/screen.
Used for third-party applications (e.g., IMDb) requiring Amazon authentication.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_LWA

enumValues.description:
"Sign in with Amazon" button on the first Pro PAP → AAP conversion interstitial
(SHOW_PRO_PAP_TO_AAP_CONVERSION). Returned when the user last signed in via an LWA handle.
Client routes to the imdb_pro_amazon_convert_linking association handle — the Amazon sign-in
step where both the "Sign in with IMDb" and "Sign in with Amazon" Pro conversion paths converge.
The "Sign in with IMDb" button on the same interstitial reuses the existing
SIGN_IN_WITH_IMDB_LINKING action.
enumValues.name: SIGN_IN_WITH_PRO_AMAZON_CONVERT_LINKING

Returns list items by increasing position order.

jumpTo: option for token-based pagination following IMDbCommonGraphletSchema standards. Jumps to a specific list item
ID and will return the "first" items starting with the provided item ID. If the provided item ID is not found, this
option will be ignored and will have the returned ListConnection's jumpToFound be false.
Will throw a BAD_USER_INPUT if used with after, last, before, or jumpToPosition.

jumpToPosition: option for index-based pagination. Jumps to a particular numerical, positive contextual position in
the list (the position after taking ListItemFilter and ListItemSort into account), and will return the "first" items
starting at the provided position value. Item positions are one-based.
If the provided jumpToPosition is 1 and the list is empty, this option will be ignored and will have the returned
ListConnection's jumpToFound be false while returning the empty list of items.
Will throw a BAD_USER_INPUT if used with after, last, before, or jumpTo, or if there are no items at the provided
position.

jumpToPosition should only be used when displaying only a single page at a time, and the entire list is not being
loaded into memory. We recommend clients to use the standard token-based pagination mechanism whenever possible.
This option is available to enable the following list features -
1. The ability to have bookmarks / links to specific points in a list for editing
2. The ability to grab list chunks in parallel

fields.description:
Individual representation records where this name is the representative,
one edge per stored representation relationship.

This is the representative-side counterpart of `representationRecords`:
the same underlying records viewed from the agent's perspective. On each
record, `client` is the represented name and `representative` is this
name (or null for records where a company represents the client without
a specific individual assigned).

Unlike `clients`, which returns at most one entry per represented name,
this field returns every record. A representative who is both the
Manager and the Publicist of the same client gets two edges, one per
relationship. Use this field when each record needs to be individually
addressable, such as contribution experiences that load and edit a
single record at a time. `total` and pagination therefore count records,
not represented names.

When `sort` is omitted, records are returned in alphabetical order of
the client's display name, equivalent to sorting by NAME ascending.
Records that share a client are returned consecutively, ordered
alphabetically by their relationship type's display text.

Up to 250 records can be requested at a time. If `first` is greater
than 250, only 250 records are returned.

Returns a connection with empty `edges` and a `total` of 0 when the
customer is not entitled, including when the customer is not logged in.

fields.description:
Vends credits for this name on titles, grouped into groupings defined by input parameter.

We group credits into "groupings" in a way that best highlights a person's work.
Appearances in a title where they were not directly involved, such as Archive Footage,
are removed from their appearance credits and moved into separate groupings.
Soundtrack credits are included within a name's credits as a separate category. This is different to a title-focused
view, where Soundtrack credits are modelled as a separate data type.
All other credit categories are presented 1-1 as groupings.

When a name has credits on individual episodes in a series, these are rolled up and presented at the series level
as a single CreditV2 value, giving a summary of their contribution. Details of individual episodes are available
from "episodeCredits" on a CreditedRole within a CreditV2 value.

When a credit has performed many roles on a title within a grouping, these are aggregated into a single CreditV2
value, with each individual role represented as a separate CreditedRole within the CreditV2.

Credits on in-development titles are only available to clients providing a Pro tier entitlement.

fields.name: employment

fields.description:
A single published endorsement this name received, addressed by its opaque
`id` (the `id` field of ProNetworkingEndorsement). Backs an addressable,
deep-link render of one endorsement without paging the full list. Only an
APPROVED endorsement ever resolves here, so a resolved endorsement's
`approvalStatus` is always APPROVED even though that enum also models PENDING.

The `id` addresses an (author → subject) endorsement slot rather than one
endorsement, so a persisted link can later resolve to a different endorsement
than the one it was created for. See ProNetworkingEndorsement.id for the reuse
semantics and for how to notice that the endorsement behind a persisted id has changed.

Resolves to null, rather than to an error, in each of the cases below, and
those cases are deliberately indistinguishable from one another:
- no endorsement has that id
- an endorsement has that id but is still awaiting the page owner's approval,
so it is visible only to its author and its subject
- the endorsement was removed or suppressed
- the endorsement belongs to a subject other than the name being queried
- the viewer is not entitled to PRO_ANY_TIER

Returning blank data instead of an error for an endorsement the viewer may not
see is deliberate: collapsing those cases into one null is what stops a caller
from confirming that endorsements it is not allowed to read exist. No business
meaning is encoded in the null: clients must infer nothing from it beyond
"nothing to render here".

Throws UNAUTHENTICATED if not logged in. A store fault raises an error instead
of silently resolving to an empty result; that error is independent of the
requested id and carries no information about whether the endorsement exists.
@entitlement(PRO_ANY_TIER)

fields.description:
Titles this name is known for.
Returns an empty list if there are no known for titles.
Titles are returned in order from most known for to least.

Each credit captures all of the roles performed by the name on a given title.
Quentin Tarantino (nm0000233) was actor, writer and director for Reservoir Dogs (tt0105236).
The Known For entry captures each of these as a separate creditedRole within the CreditV2 field.

Within a credit, creditedRoles are ordered by the category of the role. We prioritise categories linked
to the person's professions, then follow a fixed ordering of categories as seen on Title Full Credits pages
on imdb.com.

Within a category, creditedRoles are ordered by frequency of role (across episodes in a series), with alphabetical
used as a tie-breaker. The same is true for characters on appearance credits.
This behaviour differs from the ordering of creditedRoles and characters for other credits APIs (see CreditV2
documentation). The idea is to highlight the work most frequently performed by a person, therefore capturing the
work they are likely to be most recognised for on the title.

args.name: first

fields.description:
Individual representation records for this name, one edge per stored
representation relationship.

Unlike `representation`, which groups records by relationship type and
agency for display purposes, this field returns exactly one edge per
underlying record. Use this field when each record needs to be
individually addressable, such as contribution experiences that load and
edit a single record at a time. `total` and pagination therefore count
records, not groups.

Records that share a relationship type are returned consecutively. Within
a relationship type, records whose representative is the point of contact
are returned first, followed by the remaining records in alphabetical
order of their representative's display name (or their company's display
name, for records without an individual representative).

Up to 250 records can be requested at a time. If `first` is greater
than 250, only 250 records are returned.

Returns a connection with empty `edges` and a `total` of 0 when the
customer is not entitled, including when the customer is not logged in.

inputFields.description:
Defines how credits are aggregated together into a single CreditV2 result.

Aggregation allows clients to choose the level of detail to show for credits, avoiding repetition of the same
title across many roles.

Parameter is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

TITLE: All credits for a single name on a single title are aggregated together.
This supports experiences like Name Credits tab on pro.imdb.com, where all work by a name for a title is
shown together. Multiple roles on the same title are combined into a single CreditV2 with multiple CreditedRole entries.
For example, see Pulp Fiction (1994) in https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm0000233/credits.

TITLE_AND_GROUPING: Credits are broken down by title and grouping.
This reflects the same breakdown of credits seen on experiences like Name Main on imdb.com.
Each role grouping on a title gets its own CreditV2 entry, even if the person had multiple roles.
For example, for Quentin Tarantino (https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000233/), we would return three separate credits for
Pulp Fiction (1994): Director, Writer (covering two different roles) and Actor.
inputFields.name: aggregationType

inputFields.description:
Capture the order of CreditV2 items in a listing.

This is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

RELEASE_DATE: Credit ordering follows this priority sequence:
1. Release date - For singular titles, the primary release date (most recent first by default)
2. Latest release date - For series, most recent episode release date that this credit applies to
3. Title text - Alphabetical comparison of the title text
4. Title ID - A final tie-break by title ID to ensure consistent ordering (largest first).

RELEASE_DATE is the default.

The sort order can be controlled using the order parameter (ASC for oldest first, DESC for newest first).
inputFields.name: by

display name plus all non-suppressed alternate names (which already include credited-as
spellings), nicknames, and the birth/real name when present. Suppressed names are never
present in this list. Any name not in this list — including one sourced from a third party
— must be treated as disallowed.

This list is intentionally not paginated: it is returned in full so the permitted set is
unambiguous. In practice it is expected to contain well under ~50 names for any given
person (typically only a handful), so returning it in full is not a payload concern.

The API is optimized for retrieving principal credits with max-limit 30 (default 10 credits per grouping).
For complete credit lists, please use the title.creditGroupings API.

ProNetworkingEndorsement.description:
A directional endorsement: the author endorses the subject (a Name page). Each
endorsement item is a single content version with one approvalStatus; a pending
edit is its own PENDING item, separate from the APPROVED one it revises.

fields.description:
Owner-approval status which gates visibility. PENDING is a new endorsement or
a pending edit awaiting the owner's approval, visible to only the author and
the subject. APPROVED is a publicly visible endorsement.
fields.name: approvalStatus

fields.description: The endorsing member's name.
fields.name: author

fields.description:
The version ID of the currently published content for APPROVED endorsements,
or the pending content for PENDING endorsements.
fields.name: contentVersionId

fields.description:
When this endorsement's content was created. For an edited endorsement this is
the creation time of the currently-surfaced content version, not the original.
Null if the creation time is unavailable, in which case clients should omit
the date rather than treating it as an error.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
An opaque identifier for the catalog item backing this endorsement — the
identifier a contribution that removes this endorsement has to target.

Like `id`, this addresses the (author → subject) endorsement slot rather than
one endorsement: the catalog item is reused in place if the endorsement is
removed and that same author later endorses that same subject again, so a guid
can come to point at different content. A consumer that persists a guid to
issue a write later must therefore re-verify `contentVersionId` before acting
on it — the guid survives a substitution but `contentVersionId` does not. Null
on a read that did not resolve the endorsement from its catalog item.
fields.name: guid

fields.description:
An opaque concept identifier for the (author → subject) endorsement slot on
this name — not a permanent handle on one endorsement.

The identifier is reused if an endorsement is removed and that same author
later endorses that same subject again. It therefore names whichever
endorsement currently occupies that author-subject slot, not one endorsement
that was written once. Callers that persist this id (deep links, share URLs)
must expect it to later resolve to a different endorsement, or to nothing at
all. A caller that has to notice when the endorsement behind a persisted id
has changed can store `contentVersionId` alongside it: the id survives a
substitution but `contentVersionId` does not, so a changed `contentVersionId`
means the content is no longer the one the link was created for — either an
edited endorsement or a substituted one.
fields.name: id

fields.name: subject

fields.description: The subject's title credits that the author would like to endorse.

fields.description: Professions the author is endorsing the subject for.

fields.description:
The unordered set of traits associated with this profession category.
Traits are intended to be used as functional categorization markers for applying business logic.

Current possible values:
- `WORK_TYPE_CREDIT_TRAIT`. Profession categories that are typically credited on titles.
- `WORK_TYPE_EMPLOYMENT_TRAIT`. Profession categories that are linked to employment roles (e.g. Executives).
- `WORK_TYPE_REPRESENTATION_TRAIT`. Profession categories where the employed name represents clients (e.g. Talent Agents).
- `UNDERGOING_TESTING_TRAIT`. Identifies categories that are still in testing
phase and should be hidden from public-facing interfaces such as search
filters, dropdowns, and selection controls. The presence of this trait
indicates the category exists in the system but is not yet ready for general
availability in user experiences.

- filterId: Unique identifier for the filter
- constraintName: The field name to use in AdvancedNameSearchConstraints
- displayName: Human-readable filter name
- requiresEntitlement: Array of entitlements needed (e.g., ["PRO_ANY_TIER"])

fields.description:
@experimental Search for available ATS (Advanced Title Search) constraint filters by search term.

This API enables discovery of which filters can be applied to title searches. Given a search term,
it returns matching filter metadata including the filter's display name, constraint name for use
in ATS queries, and the specific values that matched the search.

For example, searching "action" returns the Genres filter with the matched term "Action" and its
constraint value. Searching "movies with producer" returns multiple filters including Title Type
(Movie, TV Movie) and Professions Attached (Producer).

Returns structured filter information including:
- filterId: Unique identifier for the filter
- constraintName: The field name to use in AdvancedTitleSearchConstraints
- displayName: Human-readable filter name
- requiresEntitlement: Array of entitlements needed (e.g., ["PRO_ANY_TIER"])
- matchedTerms: Array of matched values with displayValue (for UI), constraintValue (for queries), and searchable terms

WebLab: IMDB_SEARCH_DISCOVER_MODERN_1367402

fields.description:
Returns all localized filter options for a set of filter IDs, selecting the
appropriate Elasticsearch index based on `searchType` (TITLE → title-filters,
NAME → name-filters). Each group contains the filter's display name and all
available options with display and constraint values, translated via the Panther pipeline.

This query only covers filters that have discrete, localized option sets (e.g. genres,
title-type, profession-categories). It does not cover range-based filters (e.g. IMDbMeter
range, release date), free-form text filters (e.g. "Title name contains"), or entity
search filters (e.g. "People credited or attached", "Companies credited or attached").

The `constraintValue` for each option is always in English and is intended for use in
URL parameters (e.g. `genres=action`). The `displayValue` is the translated label for
UI presentation.

Ordering: Results are returned in the same order as the input `filterIds`. Duplicate
IDs are deduplicated; only the first occurrence is kept. Options within each group
are ordered alphabetically by `displayValue`.

Filter IDs with no matching document in the selected index are silently omitted
from the response. Returns an empty array if no filterIds match.

fields.name: names

fields.description:
Get cinemas in ascending distance from the request location.

Notes:
- If `filter.favorites` is specified as `ONLY_FAVORITES`, `filter.location.radiusInMeters` can be left as null to get all of a user's favorite cinemas.
- If both lat/long and postal code are provided to `filter.location`, the location will default to using lat/long.
- It's strongly recommended to explicitly provide startTime to avoid timezone mismatches between server and client, but if `filter.dateRange` is not provided, the startTime will default to server's 'now' and the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- If `filter.dateRange.endTime` is not provided, the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- Backwards pagination is not currently supported.

Errors:
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if `filter.location.radiusInMeters` is null AND filter.favorites` is not set to `ONLY_FAVORITES.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` with symbol `filter.location.postalCode` if the location is unknown.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if lat/long is too precise. See `LatLong` input.

Limits:
- `first` is limited to a maximum of 100. If the `first` argument exceeds the maximum, the results will be capped to the maximum.

fields.description:
Retrieve predefined user lists. Predefined User Lists have a ListClass of CHECK_INS, FAVORITE_ACTORS,
FAVORITE_THEATRES, NOT_INTERESTED, RESEARCH_NOTES, SEEN, or WATCH_LIST.

IMPORTANT: Predefined lists are NOT automatically created for users. They are created only when:
- addItemToPredefinedList mutation is called (creates list if it doesn't exist)
- createPredefinedList mutation is explicitly called

When querying for a predefined list that doesn't exist, this query returns null (does not create the list).
This distinction is critical for proper null-handling in client code to prevent infinite retry loops.

Predefined lists can be accessed by userId and list class pair as there can only be one per user for a type.
userId can be omitted only when the request is made while the authenticated user is present in the context (e.g., the user is logged in).
If the predefined list does not exist for the user, it returns null instead of throwing an exception.

fields.description:
Retrieves titles currently showing in the specified cinemas.

Notes:
- It's strongly recommended to explicitly provide startTime to avoid timezone mismatches between server and client, but if `filter.dateRange` is not provided, the startTime will default to server's 'now' and the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- If `filter.dateRange.endTime` is not provided, the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- We currently do not support pagination in existing showtimes API but hope to in the future.

Sorting:
- There is no guaranteed sort order for results returned.

Throws:
- Throws `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` if `cinemasMetadata.anyCinemaIds` is null.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if more than 400 unique cinemas are provided in `cinemasMetadata.anyCinemaIds`.

fields.description:
Returns a filtered and sorted list of lists for a user

There are two behaviors
  1. authenticated user - retrun private and public lists
  2. listOwnerUserId - return public lists owned by the user
  Note: listOwnerUserId takes precendence over the authenticated user

This query currently uses non-cached endpoint as IMDbSearchGraphlet does not support caching for List now.
This query is designed for search scenarios, leveraging the search index to deliver eventual consistency while
offering an efficient and cost effective approach to filtering and sorting user lists.

For strict consistency requirements, the following APIs offer direct access to lists from the primary data store:
1. lists API: Retrieves the lists for a user.
2. predefinedList API: Retrieves a specific predefined list for a user.
3. list API: Retrieves a single list for a list id.

Throws UNAUTHENTICATED if user is not logged in and listOwnerUserId is not provided.
Throws BAD_USER_INPUT if the listOwnerUserId is not valid.
Throws RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the listOwnerUserId doesn't exist.

fields.description:
Returns the status of a mark-all-as-watched job for the current customer.
CustomerId will be taken from x-imdb-customer-id header.
The job is identified by the customer and list, matching the input used in submitMarkAllAsWatched.

Failed jobs are safe to retry by calling submitMarkAllAsWatched again.
The system deduplicates concurrent requests so only one job runs at a time.
Automatic retries are attempted if job fails.

- Throws UNAUTHENTICATED for non-authenticated requests.
- Throws RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if no job exists for this customer and list.
- Throws VALIDATION_ERROR for unsupported listClass values.
- Throws VALIDATION_ERROR if listClass is LIST and listId is not provided.
- Throws VALIDATION_ERROR if listClass is WATCHLIST and listId is provided.

fields.description:
Returns a user's profile.

When the optional profileId is provided, the public version of that user's profile is returned.
When no profileId is provided, authentication is required and the current user's profile is returned.
This query is not cacheable when profileId is omitted for authenticated users viewing their own profile.

Possible Errors:
- Throws UNAUTHENTICATED if the user is not logged-in and no profileId is provided.
- Throws FORBIDDEN if a non-null userId is provided (userId input is blocked to prevent scraping).
- Throws BAD_USER_INPUT if the profileId resolves to an invalid userId.
- Throws RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the profileId does not resolve to an existing user.

Search_ConstraintSearchResults.description:
Results of a constraintSearch query, including matched filter constraints and a confidence score.

This is an intentionally bounded, non-paginated list. The result set is capped at 100 items
via the `first` input parameter and cursor-based pagination is not needed. The bound is stable
because filter search results are derived from a fixed set of filter definitions.

The confidence score output is a measure of how well the input search maps to constraints.
A client might use this measure when deciding if to actually use the filter constraints returned.
For example: "what movies did I watch today" might have a match (on "movies" for example)
but this maps poorly to constraints, compared to something like "action movies in italian"

fields.description:
For a given Title, returns the Title's showtimes grouped by cinema and screening type.

Notes:
- Only cinemas with showtimes for the requested title will be returned.
- If both lat/long and postal code are provided to `filter.location`, the location will default to using lat/long.
- It's strongly recommended to explicitly provide startTime to avoid timezone mismatches between server and client, but if `filter.dateRange` is not provided, the startTime will default to the server's 'now' and the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- If `filter.dateRange.endTime` is not provided, the endTime will default to `3000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- Backwards pagination is not currently supported.
- If `fallback` is not provided, there will be no fallback logic applied to the response.
- If `fallback` has `NEXT_AVAILABLE_DATE`  as it's value and the original result contains no data, the graphlet will attempt to fallback the results to the showtimes for the next available date from the provided `filter.dateRange.startTime` input value. If fallback results are found, the `fallback` results field will be non-null and provide information about the fallback result set.

Sorting:
- If `filter.location` provided, sorting will be in ascending distance from the provided location.
- If `filter.anyCinemaIds` provided, the sort order will not be guaranteed. Currently, there is no requirement to support any sort for the resulting cinemaShowtimes, since the only use case we have is for a singular cinema, which will only return a single node.

Errors:
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` with symbol `filter.location.postalCode` if the location is unknown.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if lat/long is too precise. See `LatLong` input.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if `filter.location.radiusInMeters` is null.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if both or neither `filter.anyCinemaIds` and `filter.location` are provided. Exactly one must be provided.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if both `filter.anyCinemaIds` and `fallback` are provided.
- Throws `BAD_USER_INPUT` if more than 400 unique cinemas are provided in `filter.anyCinemaIds`.

Limits:
- `first` is limited to a maximum of 100. If the `first` argument exceeds the maximum, the results will be capped to the maximum.

fields.description:
Vends name credits for this title, grouped into "Groupings" in a way that best represents a title's end credits.
Actor and Actress credits are grouped together in a 'Cast' grouping.
Archive Footage and similar roles where the person was not directly involved, are kept within this 'Cast' grouping
(which differs to how name.creditGroupings vends credits).
All other credit categories are presented 1-1 as groupings.

Groupings are presented in a fixed order, presenting groupings in an order similar to that seen
on movie or TV end credits. This field is suitable for building experiences that highlight work on a title separately
across disciplines, such as displaying all credits for a title.

When a name has credits on individual episodes in a series, these are rolled up and presented at the series level
as a single CreditV2 value, giving a summary of their contribution. Details of individual episodes are available
from "episodeCredits" on a CreditedRole within a CreditV2 value, or on the CreditV2 value.

When a credit has performed many roles on a title, these are aggregated into a single CreditV2 value, with each
individual role represented as a separate CreditedRole within the CreditV2.
This makes this field useful for building experiences where you want to show each name for a title only once.
For example, credits for The Office (2005-2013) (tt0386676) would include Mindy Kaling (nm1411676) once per grouping.
All of their roles as producer (co-executive producer, producer, and so on) are vended as a single CreditV2 value,
and separate values are given for their roles as actress, writer and director.
Note that the aggregateBy parameter can be used to disable aggregation for specific groupings.

Credits on in-development titles are only available to clients providing a Pro tier entitlement.

fields.description:
Vends name credits for this title.

When a name has credits on individual episodes in a series, these are rolled up and presented at the series level
as a single CreditV2 value, giving a summary of their contribution. Details of individual episodes are available
from "episodeCredits" on a CreditedRole within a CreditV2 value.

When a credit has performed many roles on a title, these are aggregated into a single CreditV2 value, with each
individual role represented as a separate CreditedRole within the CreditV2.
For example, credits for The Office (2005-2013) (tt0386676) would include Mindy Kaling (nm1411676) once,
listing all of their roles as producer (co-executive producer, producer, and so on), actress, writer and director
as a single CreditV2.
This makes this field useful for building experiences where you want to show each name for a title only once.
Note that the aggregateBy parameter can be used to disable aggregation for specific groupings.

Related field title.creditGroupings allows fetching credits for a title, grouped in a way that best represents
a title's end credits. When a single grouping contains large numbers of credits, additional pages of those credits
can be fetched using this field (and providing `filter.creditLevelFilter.groupings` to restrict to the grouping
being paginated).

Credits on in-development titles are only available to clients providing a Pro tier entitlement.

@entitlement(PRO_ANY_TIER)

fields.name: principalCredits

args.description:
In general: whether to utilise any entitlements passed to alter the behaviour of this API.
Specifically: For industry professionals (IMDbPro members) IMDb discloses attachment credits; which are essentially
rumored credits to in-development title that have not been publicly announced.

When false; attachments are not provided, as seen on the IMDb website.
When true; attachments are provided if the requester is entitled to receive the credits.
args.name: useEntitlement

fields.description:
Principal Credits gives the primary creative contributors to a title, organized by groupings.

We group credits in a way that highlights the primary creative roles on a title.
Showrunner, Creator and Head Writer roles are moved out of their original categories
(typically 'Producer' and 'Writer') and presented in a separate grouping per role type.
For all other credits, the grouping strategy on title.creditGroupings is followed.
Note that we label the 'Cast' grouping as 'Stars'.
Also when the TOP_CAST mode is used (see filter parameter), we vend a "Top X" or "Key X" text per grouping,
replacing the standard text.

The number of credits per grouping we vend is limited to 30, to reflect that most use cases
looking for a summary of principal credits want a limited subset of data.
For fuller data see title.creditGroupings.

Clients can control the maximum number of groupings returned using the `filter` input.
The specific groupings returned will depend on the title type
(for example giving Showrunner for TV series but not for movies, and Director for movies but not for TV series).

Note that the returned groupings may change over time, as our set of supported credit categories evolves.

Principal credits for in-development titles only available when a Pro entitlement is provided.
Without this, we only provide access to a count per grouping.

@entitlement(PRO_ANY_TIER)

TitleCreditsConstraint.description:
Example:
1. if you want to match titles with name const `nm0000138` AND `nm0000206` then specify:
`
allCredits: [{nameId: 'nm0000138'}, {nameId: 'nm0000206'}]
`

2. if you want to match titles where name const `nm0000138` was a `Director` AND `nm0000206` was a `Producer` then
specify:
`
allCredits: [{nameId: 'nm0000138', jobCategory: 'Director'}, {nameId: 'nm0000206', jobCategory: 'Producer'}]
`

3. if you want to match titles WITHOUT a `Writer` credit then specify:
`
excludeCredits: [{jobCategory: 'Writer'}]
`

4. if you want to match Titles where `nm0185819` played `James Bond` AND `nm1560977` was a `Director` then specify:
`
allCredits: [{nameId: 'nm0185819', character: 'James Bond'}, {nameId: 'nm1560977', jobCategory: 'Director'}]
`

5. if you want to match Titles where a character was called `Mario` then specifiy:
`
allCredits: [{character: 'Mario'}]
`

inputFields.description:
This is modelled as a string to allow for altering the list of allowed values over time. Supported values are:

CREDIT_IMPORTANCE: Credit ordering follows this priority sequence:
1. Grouping - Based on a fixed order of groupings, chosen to be similar to that seen on movie or TV end credits.
2. Top Stars Ranking - Priority based on special top performers list, for cast only.
3. Credited Status - Credited roles take precedence over uncredited roles.
4. Episode Count - For a series, higher episode counts appear first (names with more episodes rank higher).
5. Order - For a series, sum the order values across all episodes. For non-series, use the order value for the credit.
   (Order numbers are ignored when a large order value gap is found between 2 credits.)
6. Grouped Order - Order based on multi-level groupings, as seen in Writer category with sub-groupings.
7. Chronological Order - For a series, sort earlier start years ahead of later start years. Similar logic for end years.
8. Name Text - Alphabetical ordering by name, which typically treats "Firstname Lastname" as "Lastname, Firstname".
9. Name ID - A final tie-break by name ID to ensure consistent ordering (smallest first).

CREDIT_IMPORTANCE is the default.

The sort order can be controlled using the order parameter (ASC/DESC). When DESC (default), higher importance
credits appear first. When ASC, lower importance credits appear first.
inputFields.name: by

TitleTheatricalRentals.description:
Theatrical rental data for a title.
Entries are ordered by region code, then by earnings within each region,
following the order provided by the upstream source data (the source does not
guarantee an ascending or descending direction for earnings).

args.description:
Optional maximum number of entries to return, in the order described above.
If omitted, all entries are returned. Must be >= 0.

Intentionally optional (not the standard's `limit: Int!`): the primary
consumer renders the full table (1:1 parity with the legacy box office tab),
and the list is small and bounded (see above), so "return all" is the natural
default. `limit` is a convenience for callers that only need the top entries.
args.name: limit

fields.description:
All theatrical rental entries for this title, returned unpaginated.
This is a small bounded list backed by a frozen historical dataset
(legacy theatrical rental figures, predominantly US). Typically 1-5
entries; expected maximum well under ~50.

UIWorkflowFileUploadFormElement.description:
File upload form element. Supports both S3 and Alexandria upload modes
through a unified interface — the client upload logic is identical for both.

Client upload flow:
1. User selects file(s)
2. Client validates against fileUploadConstraints (UX hints)
3. For each file, build FormData from UIWorkflowFileUploadConfig.fields, append
file using UIWorkflowFileUploadConfig.fileFieldName, POST to
UIWorkflowFileUploadConfig.url
4. On success, client stores the UIWorkflowFileUploadResult (fileReference, fileName) as the form value
5. Client submits the workflow form via updateUIWorkflow

WatchOptionsSearchConstraint.description:
By default, watch option results are filtered to the region of the request
(determined by the x-imdb-detected-country header). Use `anyWatchRegions` to
override this with specific regions.

Gather watchProviderIds using the `watchProviders` query. Results are limited to
100 titles when filtering by non-Amazon providers.

Note: provider, mediaType, and offerType filters are evaluated independently. A title matches
if it has any watch offer satisfying each filter, but the same offer does not need to satisfy
all filters simultaneously.

Example: if you want to match titles that are available for purchase/rent on Prime Video in the US,
specify anyWatchProviderIds: ['amzn1.imdb.w2w.provider.prime_video'] AND anyWatchRegions: ['US']

Example: if you want to exclude titles that are available for physical purchase on Amazon in the UK,
specify excludeAnyWatchProviderIds: ['amzn1.imdb.w2w.provider.amazon'] AND anyWatchRegions: ['GB']

inputFields.description:
Extended IDs (eids) from CxM identity vendors (e.g. SharedID, ID5, Lotame, LiveRamp).
Used to pass 3P identity signals through to PAS for unified auction.
If not provided, no 3P identity signals will be forwarded to PAS and 3P buyers will rely
solely on their own cookie/ID matching for the impression.

These are generated client-side via CxM identity scripts. We treat these IDs as passthrough for PAS/AAX

Up to four different identifiers present in this field at launch, with the possibility of a fifth
later on. There is no maximum array size

Example:
extendedIds: [
  { source: "pubcid.org", userIds: [{ id: "e52a-4033-b54c-f67d", agentType: 1 }] },
  { source: "id5-sync.com", userIds: [{ id: "ID5-ZHMO_gMpLk...", agentType: 1 }] },
  { source: "crwdcntrl.net", userIds: [{ id: "pan-id-abc123", agentType: 1 }] },
  { source: "liveramp.com", userIds: [{ id: "AsvkAsvQTfYZ...", agentType: 3 }] }
]
inputFields.name: extendedIds

inputFields.description:

request for third-party bidder targeting in the unified auction.
If not provided, site.ref will not be set.

YearRangeInput.description:
Represents a range of years for filtering filmography credits.
Both fields are optional. If both are omitted, no filtering is applied.

inputFields.description:
The end year of the range (inclusive).
If omitted, matches all years from startYear onwards.
Must be non-negative. Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if value is negative.
Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if endYear < startYear.
inputFields.name: endYear

inputFields.description:
The start year of the range (inclusive).
If omitted, matches all years up to and including endYear.
Must be non-negative. Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if value is negative.
Throws GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED if startYear > endYear.
inputFields.name: startYear
